title: Rank-unimodality conjecture for principal permutation-pattern downsets
statement: Let $\rho$ be a permutation, and let $D(\rho)$ be the principal downset of all permutations contained in $\rho$, ordered by permutation-pattern containment and ranked by permutation length. A ranked poset is rank-unimodal when its rank sizes form a unimodal sequence. **Rank-unimodality conjecture for principal downsets.** Every principal downset in the permutation pattern poset is rank-unimodal. This is presented as an unresolved unimodality problem; the general case remains open.
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2108.12979](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12979), [arXiv:1403.1527](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1527), [arXiv:1305.5569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.5569).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).
